newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. consul criticises Israeli residency policy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. consul criticises Israeli residency policy.

text.p: A U.S. diplomat said on Wednesday that Israel was discriminating against Americans of Palestinian origin in Jerusalem by threatening to deprive them of residency rights unless they gave up their U.S. passports.

U.S. Consul General Edward Abington said his office had complained to Israel after receiving more than 65 complaints from Palestinian-Americans who live in Arab East Jerusalem, occupied by Israel since 1967.
"We had five meetings with Israeli officials and sent them 12 letters on the issue, but their response to us had been there's no such policy," Abington told Reuters.

Human rights organisations and PLO officials have repeatedly accused Israel of trying to make East Jerusalem predominantly Jewish by confiscating the residency permits of Palestinians who have dual nationality.

"We are trying to protect our citizens and we assure Palestinian-Americans that under U.S. law, it is impossible for a U.S. citizen to lose U.S. citizenship involuntarily, by force or duress," Abington said.
"This policy is tied very much to Americans of Palestinian origin, Israeli-Americans don't have the same treatment," he said.

Faisal al-Husseini, the PLO-appointed official in charge of Palestinian affairs in Jerusalem, had said that as many as 2,000 Arabs in East Jerusalem had been affected by Israel's permit confiscation policy.

"I know that other consulates in Jerualem have received the same complaints. Thousands of Palestinians with dual nationalities live here, have been born here and have lives here yet are asked to give up their nationalities," Abington said.
The Israeli Interior Ministry did not comment despite several requests from Reuters to respond to the allegations.

The U.S. Consulate published an advertisement in Palestinian newspapers on Tuesday asking Palestinian-Americans to contact it if they are coerced by Israel to renounce their U.S. citizenship or surrender their American passports.

"The objective of the ad is to assure people because as a result of this policy we have a lot of people who are very afraid to go back to the U.S. to visit dying relatives or for study and business," Abington said.
